Answer_with_writing_sample: The income tax department has several mechanisms in place to track unreported rental income, even if you choose not to declare it in your Income Tax Return (ITR). Firstly, there’s the concept of TDS (Tax Deducted at Source); if your tenant is a corporate entity or a high-value individual, they are likely required to deduct TDS on the rent paid and deposit it with the government. This creates a paper trail that the income tax department can easily trace back to you. Moreover, the department has access to various databases and information-sharing agreements, which means they can cross-reference data collected from property registrations, bank transactions, and even online rental platforms. This is all part of their efforts to curb tax evasion and ensure that all income is reported accurately. Additionally, if your rental income is substantial, it may trigger scrutiny during audits or data investigations, particularly if there are discrepancies in your other reported income sources. Lastly, keep in mind that if you are ever flagged for audits and it turns out you have not reported your rental income, you will not only face penalties but also interest on the unpaid tax. So, while you may think you can fly under the radar, the reality is that the income tax department has multiple ways to connect the dots. It’s always wiser to report accurately and take advantage of the deductions available for expenses related to your rental property instead of risking penalties.
